column1: # Lithuanian nouns that occur as direct address (vocative, šauksmininkas).
# word <TAB> gloss (optional). Lines starting with # are ignored. An empty file
# switches the vocative rule off. Written without Lithuanian diacritics;
# matching strips them, so "teti" also matches "tėti".
# Why a list is needed: Lithuanian has a separate vocative case, spelled like
# the nominative for many nouns but accented differently - "mama" (mother) is
# mamà when talking about her and mãma when talking to her. Neither source
# behind lt_kirciai.tsv can express that: the dictionary holds one entry per
# spelling (189262 forms, 189262 distinct spellings, not one duplicate), and
# the annotated corpus it is built from does not separate the two cases.
# Why punctuation alone is not enough: a vocative is almost always fenced off
# by commas, but "Vaje vaje, kiek daug telpa tame žodyje mama" has the comma
# and no vocative. A word is treated as address only when it is on this list
# AND fenced on both sides by a comma or the sentence edge.
# The list is deliberately short: missing a vocative only loses an
# improvement, while a false positive mis-accents an ordinary word.
